pull.title: net, http: handle socket errors separately from reads
pull.body:
`poll()` reports an error or hangup on a socket whether or not we asked for it. If that happens for a peer we did not request to read from, disconnect directly. This just adds clarity: previously we would attempt a send that would then fail. The only side-effect is a changed log message. Nothing changes with `select()`: since #36716 it no longer reports errors for established connections.

The last commit does the same for HTTP, where on error it also no longer attempts a final read from a client whose reads are paused.

As a followup to #36716, `p2p_socket_errors.py` adds coverage for existing behavior:
- the node ignores a single urgent byte: the connection stays open, ordinary data is still processed and the urgent byte is not counted as received.
- a peer reset while the node is sending (the change above only changes the log message)

Similarly `interface_http.py` checks that:
- a single urgent byte does not disturb an ordinary request.
- a client reset while the server has unsent responses (the HTTP change only changes the log message)

Two commits only move code:
- the send-stall wait moves from `p2p_ping_ibd.py` into the test framework, so the new tests can use it.
- the `wait_ignores_urgent_data` unit test from #36716 moves next to the other wait test. It was placed above the socket pair tests there to ease backporting.

author Sjors Provoost <sjors@sprovoost.nl> 1795614957 +0100
committer Sjors Provoost <sjors@sprovoost.nl> 1795617276 +0100

net: only use the select error set while connecting

Windows uses the select() error set to report a failed non-blocking
connect(). Make ErrorEvent an event that can be requested from
Sock::Wait(), like RecvEvent and SendEvent: with select() it adds the
socket to the error set. ConnectToSocket() requests it while
connecting. This is safe on all platforms, as any error condition is
worth waking for there.

All other uses of select() now leave the error set empty. With
select(), sockets waited on without ErrorEvent no longer wake up for
or report exceptional conditions, such as TCP urgent data on an
established connection. No behavior change with poll().

Add a unit test: with an urgent byte pending, waiting for RecvEvent
must not report ErrorEvent.

Co-authored-by: Cory Fields <cory-nospam-@coryfields.com>
Co-authored-by: Vasil Dimov <vd@FreeBSD.org>

net: disconnect on poll errors before sending

Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP when no read was requested,
skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect
the peer. This also changes the debug log message.

Co-authored-by: Cory Fields <cory-nospam-@coryfields.com>
